records.literal_gloss: Not let be troubled of you the heart; believe in the God, and in me believe.

en.L: "Do not let your heart be troubled; believe in God, and believe in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} also.
en.B: "Do not let your hearts be troubled. Believe in God, and believe in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as well.
en.R: "Do not let your hearts be troubled. Believe in God. Believe in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} too.

es.B: «Que no se angustie {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} corazón. {{plural_you:Crean|Creed}} en Dios, y {{plural_you:crean|creed}} también en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: «No {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que nada {{plural_you:los|os}} angustie. {{plural_you:Crean|Creed}} en Dios. {{plural_you:Crean|Creed}} también en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

fr.B: « Ne laissez pas le trouble envahir vos cœurs. Croyez en Dieu, et croyez de même en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.

vi.B: "Các con đừng để lòng mình bối rối. Hãy tin vào Đức Chúa Trời, và cũng hãy tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: "너희 마음이 흔들리지 않게 하여라. 하나님을 믿어라. 그리고 나를 믿어라.
ko.B: "너희는 마음이 흔들리지 않게 하여라. 하나님을 믿고, 나도 믿어라.
ko.R: "두려워하거나 걱정하지 마라. 하나님을 믿어라. 나도 믿어라.

decisions.choice: be troubled: shaken, stirred up with fear and distress
decisions.reason: The same verb was used of Jesus himself at the tomb of Lazarus (11:33), when he spoke of his coming hour (12:27), and when he announced the betrayal (13:21). He has just told the disciples that he is leaving, that one of them will betray him and that Peter will deny him (13:21-38). Now he tells them not to be shaken by it. He says the same again in 14:27.

decisions.choice: your heart: one heart for the whole group
alternatives: each person's heart, considered one by one
decisions.reason: "Your" is plural and "heart" is singular. The heart is the inner person, where fear and trust live. The singular speaks of the disciples together, as one group facing the same loss; it means the heart of each of them.

decisions.choice: believe ... believe: both are commands
alternatives: You believe in God; believe also in me
You believe in God, and you believe in me
Believe in God, and you believe in me
decisions.reason: The Greek form of the verb is the same for "you believe" and "believe!", so either could be a statement or a command. Reading both as commands fits the command just before ("let your heart not be troubled") and the later call to believe in 14:11. Another common reading takes the first as a statement and the second as a command: "You believe in God; believe also in me." The two clauses stand in a mirror pattern (believe in God / in me believe), which puts trust in Jesus beside trust in God. Either way the point is the same: the cure for a troubled heart is trust in God and in Jesus together.

decisions.choice: Do not let your heart be troubled (L); Do not let your hearts be troubled (B, R)
alternatives: Let not your heart be troubled
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the singular "heart"; Balanced and Readable say "hearts", since English uses the plural when several people are meant (meaning decision m2). The same Greek words return in 14:27, and every level gives them the same English there, so the reader sees Jesus close the thought where he began it.

decisions.choice: su corazón, singular
decisions.reason: One heart for the whole group (meaning decision m2); Spanish says it this way naturally.

decisions.choice: crean ... crean, both commands
decisions.reason: Both verbs are taken as commands (meaning decision m3), which the Spanish imperative shows.

decisions.choice: Ne laissez pas le trouble envahir vos cœurs (B); Ne soyez pas bouleversés (R)
alternatives: Que votre cœur ne se trouble pas
decisions.reason: The verb means shaken and stirred up with fear (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the singular "cœur" (m2); Balanced uses the plural, as French does for several people. In French "cœur" is mostly the seat of feeling, so Readable says the plain "bouleversés", which carries both the shock and the distress; "inquiets" would be too weak.

decisions.choice: moyo wenu usifadhaike (L); mioyo yenu isifadhaike (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has one heart for the whole group (meaning note m2), which Literal keeps; Balanced and Readable say "hearts", as the English does. "Kufadhaika" is the verb used of Jesus himself at 11:33, 12:27 and 13:21. Both "believe" verbs are commands, "mwaminini ... niaminini". The same in verse 27.

decisions.choice: tin vào
decisions.reason: The key term "believe" keeps the verb "tin" at every level, with "vào" for the construction with eis. Vietnamese "lòng" has no number, so the English choice between "heart" and "hearts" does not arise.

decisions.choice: Ta ... các con (Jesus to the disciples)
decisions.reason: As set for the whole book: Jesus says "Ta" of himself (the deity_pronoun span in mid-sentence) and "các con" to his disciples. Recorded once for this passage.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean; Jesus speaks to the disciples in the plain style (해라체), the disciples answer in 합쇼체, and Literal keeps the historic present in narrative (14:5-9)
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change (style guide, section 7); respect for Jesus is carried by "께서" and -시- in narrative. Speech levels as in the style guide, section 4. Recorded once for 14:1-14.

decisions.choice: "흔들리지 않게 하여라" (L, B); "두려워하거나 걱정하지 마라" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the verb as being shaken with fear and distress; "흔들리다" pictures the shaking, and Readable names the feelings plainly. The older "근심하지 말라" is avoided as the wording of familiar versions.

source.text: ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ τοῦ πατρός μου μοναὶ πολλαί εἰσιν· εἰ δὲ μή, εἶπον ἂν ὑμῖν ὅτι πορεύομαι ἑτοιμάσαι τόπον ὑμῖν·

records.literal_gloss: In the house of the Father of me dwelling places many are; if but not, I would have told you, because I go to prepare a place for you;

en.L: In the house of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father there are many dwelling places; but if not, I would have told you, for I go to prepare a place for you.
en.B: There are many dwelling places in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father's house. Otherwise I would have told you, for I am going to prepare a place for you.
en.R: There are many places to live in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father's house. If that were not true, I would have told you. In fact, I am going there to get a place ready for you.

es.L: En la casa de mi Padre hay muchas moradas; y si no, {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} habría dicho, porque voy a preparar{{plural_you:les|os}} un lugar.
es.B: En la casa de mi Padre hay muchas moradas. Si no fuera así, {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} habría dicho, porque voy a preparar{{plural_you:les|os}} un lugar.
es.R: En la casa de mi Padre hay muchos lugares donde vivir. Si no fuera así, {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} habría dicho. De hecho, voy allá a preparar{{plural_you:les|os}} un lugar.

fr.L: Dans la maison de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père, il y a de nombreuses demeures ; sinon, je vous l’aurais dit, car je m’en vais préparer un lieu pour vous.
fr.B: Il y a de nombreuses demeures dans la maison de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père. S’il n’en était pas ainsi, je vous l’aurais dit, car je pars vous y préparer une place.
fr.R: Dans la maison de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père, il y a beaucoup d’endroits où habiter. Si ce n’était pas vrai, je vous l’aurais dit. D’ailleurs, je vais là-bas pour vous préparer une place.

sw.L: Katika nyumba ya Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kuna makao mengi; kama sivyo, ningaliwaambia, kwa maana ninakwenda kuwaandalia mahali.
sw.B: Katika nyumba ya Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kuna makao mengi. La sivyo ningewaambia, kwa maana ninakwenda kuwaandalia mahali.

vi.L: Trong nhà Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} có nhiều chỗ ở; nếu không, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói với các con rồi, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi để dọn chỗ cho các con.
vi.B: Trong nhà Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} có nhiều chỗ ở. Nếu không phải vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói với các con rồi, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi để chuẩn bị chỗ cho các con.
vi.R: Trong nhà Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} có nhiều chỗ để ở. Nếu không phải như vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói cho các con biết rồi. Thật ra, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đến đó để chuẩn bị chỗ cho các con.

ko.L: 내 아버지의 집에는 머무를 곳이 많다. 그렇지 않다면 내가 너희에게 말했을 것이다. 내가 너희를 위하여 자리를 마련하러 가기 때문이다.
ko.B: 내 아버지의 집에는 머무를 곳이 많다. 그렇지 않다면 내가 너희에게 말해 주었을 것이다. 나는 너희를 위해 자리를 마련하러 가는 것이다.
ko.R: 내 아버지의 집에는 살 곳이 많다. 그렇지 않다면 내가 너희에게 말해 주었을 것이다. 사실 나는 너희가 있을 곳을 준비하러 거기에 간다.

decisions.choice: my Father's house: the Father's own home, where he is present
decisions.reason: In 2:16 "my Father's house" was the temple in Jerusalem, but Jesus is now speaking of where he is going: to the Father (13:1, 3; 14:12). The picture is of a large family house with room for many. It speaks of being with the Father, as the next verse says ("so that where I am, you also may be").

decisions.choice: dwelling places: places to stay and live, lasting homes
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb "remain" (or "stay"), which John uses often (1:38-39; 15:4-10). It means a place where one stays, not a place one passes through. In 14:23 the same noun returns: the Father and the Son will come and make their dwelling with the one who loves Jesus. So the hope of being with the Father later is matched by his presence now.

decisions.choice: a statement: If it were not so, I would have told you, for I am going to prepare a place for you
alternatives: If it were not so, would I have told you that I am going to prepare a place for you?
If it were not so, I would have told you that I go to prepare a place for you
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT punctuates this as a statement, and that is followed here. The linking word is then read as "for": Jesus would have warned them if there were no room, and his going to prepare a place shows that there is. Other editions put a question mark at the end and read the linking word as "that": "If it were not so, would I have told you that I am going to prepare a place for you?" The point is the same either way: Jesus has not misled them.

decisions.choice: the linking word (for / that) is read
decisions.reason: The oldest manuscripts have the small linking word before "I go"; many later manuscripts lack it, giving "If it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you." The SBLGNT includes it. A reviewer should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: dwelling places (L, B); places to live (R)
decisions.reason: The older English "mansions" once meant simply "places to stay" but now suggests large, grand houses, which the Greek word does not mean (meaning decision m2). "Rooms" is also possible but loses the sense of a lasting home.

decisions.choice: Otherwise (B); If that were not true (R); In fact, I am going there to get a place ready (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced puts "if not" in one natural word. Readable breaks the sentence and shows the link with "In fact": his going to prepare a place is the proof that there is room (meaning decision m3). "There" is supplied: the place is in the Father's house.

decisions.choice: moradas (L, B); lugares donde vivir (R)
decisions.reason: Lasting places to live (meaning decision m2). "Morada" comes back in 14:23, so Literal and Balanced keep the link.

decisions.choice: demeures (L, B); endroits où habiter (R)
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb "remain" (meaning decision m2), and French "demeure" comes from "demeurer", the verb used for "remain" in 14:10 and 15:4-10, so the link stays visible and returns in 14:23. "Demeure" can also name a fine residence, as English "mansion" does, but beside "la maison de mon Père" it reads as a place to live; a reviewer may weigh that. "Chambres" would make the house a hotel. Readable says what the word means in plain words.

decisions.choice: makao (L, B); mahali pa kuishi (R)
decisions.reason: "Makao" are places where one stays and lives, lasting homes, the sense in the meaning note, and the same word serves in verse 23, where the Greek repeats it. "Vyumba" (rooms) would make it a building plan.

decisions.choice: chỗ ở
decisions.reason: Monai are lasting places to stay; "chỗ ở" says that without picturing rooms in a building.

decisions.choice: "머무를 곳" (L, B); "살 곳" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek noun is from the verb "remain" (menō), which Korean renders "머무르다" through John; "머무를 곳" keeps that link. "방" (room) is too small for the meaning decision's lasting homes, and "거할 곳" is the wording of familiar versions.

source.text: καὶ ἐὰν πορευθῶ καὶ ἑτοιμάσω τόπον ὑμῖν, πάλιν ἔρχομαι καὶ παραλήμψομαι ὑμᾶς πρὸς ἐμαυτόν, ἵνα ὅπου εἰμὶ ἐγὼ καὶ ὑμεῖς ἦτε.

records.literal_gloss: And if I go and prepare a place for you, again I come and will take along you to myself, so that where am I also you may be.

en.L: And if I go and prepare a place for you, I am coming again, and I will take you to {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}, so that where I am, you also may be.
en.B: And when I have gone and prepared a place for you, I will come back and take you to be with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, so that you also may be where I am.
en.R: After I go and get a place ready for you, I will come back. I will take you to be with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, so that you will be where I am.

es.L: Y si me voy y {{plural_you:les|os}} preparo un lugar, vengo otra vez y {{plural_you:los|os}} tomaré conmigo, para que donde yo estoy, también {{plural_you:ustedes estén|vosotros estéis}}.
es.B: Y cuando me haya ido y {{plural_you:les|os}} haya preparado un lugar, volveré y {{plural_you:los|os}} llevaré conmigo, para que también {{plural_you:ustedes estén|vosotros estéis}} donde yo estoy.
es.R: Después de irme y preparar{{plural_you:les|os}} un lugar, volveré. {{plural_you:Los|Os}} llevaré conmigo, para que {{plural_you:ustedes estén|vosotros estéis}} donde yo estoy.

fr.L: Et si je pars et vous prépare un lieu, je viens de nouveau et je vous prendrai auprès de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, afin que là où je suis, vous aussi, vous soyez.
fr.B: Et quand je serai allé vous préparer une place, je reviendrai et je vous emmènerai auprès de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, pour que vous aussi, vous soyez là où je suis.
fr.R: Quand je serai parti vous préparer une place, je reviendrai. Je vous emmènerai avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et vous serez là où je suis.

vi.L: Và nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi và dọn chỗ cho các con, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} lại đến, và sẽ đem các con về với chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, để {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở đâu thì các con cũng ở đó.
vi.B: Khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã đi và chuẩn bị chỗ cho các con rồi, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ trở lại và đem các con về với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, để {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở đâu thì các con cũng ở đó.
vi.R: Sau khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi và chuẩn bị chỗ cho các con, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ trở lại. Ta sẽ đem các con về ở với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, để các con được ở nơi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở.

ko.L: 그리고 내가 가서 너희를 위하여 자리를 마련하면, 다시 온다. 그리고 너희를 나 자신에게로 데려갈 것이다. 내가 있는 곳에 너희도 있게 하려는 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 가서 너희를 위해 자리를 마련하면, 다시 와서 너희를 내게로 데려가겠다. 그래서 내가 있는 곳에 너희도 함께 있게 하겠다.
ko.R: 나는 가서 너희가 있을 곳을 준비한 다음 다시 올 것이다. 그리고 너희를 데려가 나와 함께 있게 할 것이다. 그러면 너희도 내가 있는 곳에 있게 된다.

decisions.choice: if I go: a condition that is sure to be met
alternatives: a real doubt whether he will go
decisions.reason: Jesus has said that he is going (13:33, 36; 14:2). The "if" does not raise a doubt about it; it sets out what will follow once it has happened, much like "when".

decisions.choice: I am coming again: his return to bring them to be with him
alternatives: his coming to the disciples after the resurrection only
his coming through the Spirit only
his coming for each believer at death
decisions.reason: The present tense speaks of a sure future. Taking the disciples to himself, so that they will be where he is, points most naturally to his coming at the end, when he brings his people to be with him (compare 21:22-23; 17:24). This same chapter also speaks of other comings: after the resurrection (14:18-19) and in the presence of the Father and the Son with those who love him (14:23). John may intend these to be heard together; the words here do not settle when.

decisions.choice: take you to myself: take you along to be with me
decisions.reason: The verb means to take someone along with oneself, to receive someone into one's company. The stress falls on being with Jesus, which the purpose clause spells out.

decisions.choice: where I am, you also may be: an answer to 13:33, 36
decisions.reason: Jesus told the disciples that they could not come where he was going, not now, but later (13:33, 36). Here he says how "later" will happen. He prays for the same in 17:24, and he said it of anyone who serves him in 12:26.

decisions.choice: when I have gone (B); After I go (R); I will come back and take you to be with me (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "when" or "after" because the condition is certain (meaning decision m1). "Come back" gives the sense of "again", and "to be with me" says plainly what "to myself" means (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: cuando me haya ido (B); Después de irme (R); volveré y los llevaré conmigo
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decisions m1, m3).

decisions.choice: je viens de nouveau (L); je reviendrai (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek present speaks of a sure future (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps the present, with "de nouveau" for "again"; Balanced and Readable use the future, which is how French states a promise. Balanced and Readable also say "quand" for the condition that is sure to be met (m1).

source.text: καὶ ὅπου ἐγὼ ὑπάγω οἴδατε τὴν ὁδόν.

es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes conocen|Vosotros conocéis}} el camino para llegar adonde yo voy».

fr.R: Vous connaissez le chemin pour aller là où je vais. »

vi.R: Các con biết đường đến nơi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi."

ko.R: 너희는 내가 가는 곳으로 가는 길을 안다."

decisions.choice: the shorter text: where I am going, you know the way
alternatives: And where I am going you know, and the way you know
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read a longer sentence: "And where I go you know, and the way you know." The shorter text is found in the oldest manuscripts and is the reading of the SBLGNT. The longer one seems to smooth out the short, compressed sentence. A reviewer should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the way: the road that leads to where Jesus is going
decisions.reason: Jesus uses an ordinary word for a road or path, and Thomas takes it that way (verse 5). Verse 6 shows what Jesus means: he himself is the way to the Father, and the disciples already know him.

decisions.choice: Lord: a disciple's address to his master
decisions.reason: Thomas is one of the disciples who follow Jesus (11:16), so the word is "Lord", as with Peter in 13:36-37 and Philip in verse 8.

decisions.choice: Thomas takes "the way" as a road to a place
decisions.reason: Like Peter in 13:36-37, Thomas thinks of a place one could travel to. He does not know where Jesus is going, so he cannot see how they could know the road. His honest question opens the way for Jesus's answer in verse 6. Thomas speaks his doubts plainly elsewhere too (11:16; 20:24-25).

decisions.choice: how can we know the way
alternatives: how do we know the way?
decisions.reason: Some important early manuscripts have a shorter question: "how do we know the way?" The SBLGNT reads "how are we able to know the way?" The meaning is the same. A reviewer should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: says (L); said (B, R); also verses 6, 8 and 9
decisions.reason: John often tells past events in the present tense ("says") to make a scene vivid. Literal keeps the present; Balanced and Readable use the past, as stories are normally told. This applies to every such verb in the passage ("says" in verses 5, 6, 8 and 9).

decisions.choice: Then how can we know the way to get there?
decisions.reason: Readable adds "Then" and "to get there" to show how Thomas's second sentence follows from the first: without knowing the place, he cannot know the road to it.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal; pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in John: Literal keeps John's present ("dice", "ven"); Balanced and Readable use the pretérito. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: Señor
decisions.reason: A disciple's address to his master (meaning decision m1), as elsewhere in John.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping John’s present tense ("dit"); passé composé (R); speech in its own tenses at every level
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
the present tense throughout at Literal
decisions.reason: The French brief for the passage (14:1-14), as in 1:19. The few narrative lines (verses 5, 6, 8, 9) are introduced by John’s present "says"; Literal keeps it, which with "dire" looks the same as the passé simple; Balanced uses the passé simple ("répondit") and Readable the passé composé ("a dit", "a répondu"). Jesus’s words keep their own tenses at every level.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (anamwambia, here and in verses 6, 8, 9 and 22); past at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As in the earlier chapters, for the whole of chapter 14.

decisions.choice: I am the way: one of Jesus's sayings that begin "I am" with a picture
decisions.reason: Here "I am" has a predicate, like "I am the bread of life" (6:35), "I am the light of the world" (8:12), "I am the good shepherd" (10:11) and "I am the resurrection and the life" (11:25). The sentence is ordinary in form, but the "I" is stressed: Jesus does not show the way as a guide does; he is the way. He answers Thomas's question about the road with himself.

decisions.choice: the way, and the truth, and the life: the way comes first, and the other two say why he is the way
alternatives: three equal titles with no order among them
a single idea: the true and living way
decisions.reason: Thomas asked about the way, and the next clause explains only the way ("no one comes to the Father except through me"), so "the way" is the main point. "Truth" and "life" say what makes Jesus the way: in him the truth about God is made known (1:14, 17-18; 8:32; 18:37), and in him is the life that comes from God (1:4; 5:26; 11:25). The three are still three nouns joined by "and", each with its article, so each is said of Jesus in its own right.

decisions.choice: No one comes to the Father except through me: Jesus is the only access to the Father
decisions.reason: "Comes to the Father" means coming to God himself, to know him and be with him, which is where Jesus is going (verses 2-4, 12). Only the Son, who has seen the Father, can make him known (1:18; 6:46); compare "I am the door" (10:9). The next verse ties coming to the Father with knowing Jesus.

decisions.choice: I am the way, the truth, and the life (B); I am the way, and I am the truth and the life (R); Only through me does anyone come to the Father (B); The only way anyone can come to the Father is through me (R)
alternatives: I am the way and the truth and the life (B)
No one comes to the Father except through me (B, R)
decisions.reason: "I am the way, the truth, and the life" is the plain English of the Greek; there is no other natural way to say it, and it is the form readers know. The second sentence is put in our own words at Balanced and Readable, which both put "through me" in the place of stress; "answered" is a past tense for the historic present (14:5 r-en-1). Readable repeats "I am" to set the way first (meaning decision m2) and states the second sentence positively. Literal keeps each "and".

decisions.choice: el camino, la verdad y la vida (B); el camino, y soy la verdad y la vida (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable shows that the way comes first (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: le chemin
decisions.reason: Thomas has just asked about the road (14:4-5), and Jesus answers with the same ordinary word (meaning decisions m1 and m2). "Chemin" keeps that link in French, where "la voie" sounds more abstract and loses the echo of Thomas’s question. "Lui" here is Thomas and has no setting.

decisions.choice: Mimi ni njia, na kweli, na uzima
decisions.reason: "Mimi ni ...", as in the other sayings with a picture (6:35, 8:12, 10:7, 10:11, 11:25). "Kweli" for truth and "uzima" for life, as throughout John; "kupitia" for "through".

decisions.choice: đường đi (L), con đường (B, R); chân lý; sự sống
decisions.reason: "Chân lý" and "sự sống" are the book-wide key terms for truth and life. "Đường" keeps the picture of a road, which Thomas has just asked about.

decisions.choice: "길이고 진리이고 생명이다" (L); "바로 길이며 진리이며 생명이다" (B); "오다" for "comes" at every level
decisions.reason: Modern endings replace the archaic "-이요 ... -이니" of familiar versions; Balanced marks the emphatic "I" with "바로". Korean keeps the Greek "comes": Jesus speaks as one who belongs with the Father.

decisions.choice: If you had known me, you would have known my Father also
alternatives: If you have come to know me, you will know my Father also
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads a condition contrary to fact, which gently rebukes the disciples: they have not yet truly known Jesus. Some early manuscripts, including one of the oldest papyri and Codex Sinaiticus, read a promise instead: "If you have come to know me, you will know my Father also." Both readings are old, and the promise fits the encouragement of the rest of the verse. The SBLGNT reading is followed. A reviewer should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: a condition contrary to fact: they have not yet fully known him
decisions.reason: The form says that they had not known Jesus as he truly is, and so had not known the Father in him. This does not deny that they know him at all (verse 4: "you know the way"). Two different verbs for "know" are used in the two halves; here they mean the same.

decisions.choice: from now on: from this hour of Jesus's going to the Father
alternatives: from the time they first met Jesus
decisions.reason: The hour of his glory has come (13:31-32). From now on the disciples know the Father and have seen him, because they have seen Jesus, as verse 9 explains (compare 1:18; 12:45). "Have seen" is a perfect: they have seen, and it stays true.

decisions.choice: truly known; But from now on you do know him
decisions.reason: Readable adds "truly" to show that the rebuke is about knowing Jesus fully, not about knowing him at all (meaning decision m2), and "But" to show the turn from rebuke to promise.

decisions.choice: de verdad; sí lo conocen
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: hẳn cũng đã biết
decisions.reason: Vietnamese has no verb form for a condition contrary to fact; "hẳn" (surely would have) marks that they have not yet fully known him.

decisions.choice: show us the Father: a request to see God
decisions.reason: Philip asks to see the Father with his eyes. The request recalls Moses asking God, "Show me your glory" (Exodus 33:18), and God answering that no one can see his face and live (Exodus 33:20). John has already said that no one has ever seen God, but the Son has made him known (1:18). Jesus's answer in verse 9 turns on this.

decisions.choice: it is enough for us: we will be satisfied and ask nothing more
decisions.reason: The verb means "to be sufficient". Philip means that one sight of the Father would settle every question.

decisions.choice: we will need nothing more (B); let us see the Father. That is all we ask (R)
alternatives: and it is enough for us
and that will be enough for us
decisions.reason: "It is enough for us" is said in natural English. Readable says "let us see" to make plain that Philip asks for a sight of God (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: no necesitamos nada más (B); Es todo lo que pedimos (R)
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: "뵙게 해 주십시오" (R)
decisions.reason: "뵙다" is the humble verb for seeing someone honoured; Philip speaks of God the Father.

decisions.choice: so long a time I am with you: a state that began in the past and still goes on
decisions.reason: The Greek uses the present "I am" with a phrase of time for something that has been true for a long time and is still true. Jesus has been with the disciples since the beginning (1:35-51).

decisions.choice: with you (all) ... you (Philip) have not known me
decisions.reason: "With you" is plural: Jesus has been with all the disciples. "You have not known" is singular and is spoken to Philip by name. Philip's question stands for the whole group, as the plural "you" in verses 7 and 10-11 shows.

decisions.choice: known me: known who I truly am
decisions.reason: Philip knows Jesus as a person, but has not grasped who he is: the one in whom the Father is seen (verse 9b; verse 7). The perfect tense means "have come to know and now know".

decisions.choice: I have been with you all this time (B); I have been with all of you for such a long time (R); Do you still not know who I am? (R)
alternatives: So long a time I am with you
Have I been with you so long
decisions.reason: English uses "have been" for the Greek present with a phrase of time (meaning decision m1). Readable says "all of you" for the plural and adds "who I am" to show what kind of knowing is meant (meaning decision m3); "answered" is a past tense for the historic present (14:5 r-en-1).

decisions.choice: con ustedes (plural) ... no me has conocido (singular)
decisions.reason: Spanish shows the shift from all of them to Philip alone (meaning decision m2); only the plural takes the setting.

decisions.choice: je suis avec vous depuis ... (present tense at every level)
alternatives: il y a si longtemps que j’ai été avec vous
decisions.reason: Like the Greek, French uses the present with "depuis" for a state that began in the past and still goes on (meaning decision m1), so every level keeps the present, where English needs "I have been". "Vous" is plural and "tu" singular, as in the Greek (m2), so French shows the shift to Philip without help; Readable still adds "tous", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "các con" (with you all) and "con" (you, Philip)
decisions.reason: The Greek moves from plural to singular; Vietnamese marks the same shift with "các con" and "con".

decisions.choice: "너희" (with you all) and "너" (you, Philip) kept apart
decisions.reason: The Greek moves from the plural to the singular (meaning decision); Korean has the same two pronouns and keeps the contrast at every level.

decisions.choice: whoever has seen me has seen the Father: the Father is seen in the Son
decisions.reason: Jesus said the same in public: "the one who sees me sees the one who sent me" (12:45). The Son, who is close to the Father's heart, has made him known (1:18). This does not mean that the Son and the Father are the same person; verse 10 explains it: the Father is in the Son and does his works through him. So Philip's request has already been answered.

decisions.choice: has seen: a seeing that has happened and still counts
decisions.reason: Both verbs are perfects. Whoever has seen Jesus has really seen, and goes on having seen, the Father.

decisions.choice: how can you say: surprise and gentle rebuke
decisions.reason: The "you" is stressed: after all this time, Philip of all people. The question does not ask for an answer; it shows that the request is out of place.

decisions.choice: To have seen me is to have seen the Father (B); If you have seen me, you have seen the Father (R); why are you asking me to show you the Father? (R)
alternatives: Whoever has seen me has seen the Father
How can you say, 'Show us the Father'?
decisions.reason: "The one who has seen" means anyone at all; Balanced and Readable say it in forms that need no pronoun. Readable turns the quoted request into ordinary speech.

decisions.choice: ¿Cómo dices {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} ...?
decisions.reason: The stressed "tú" carries the gentle rebuke (meaning decision m3). It is Philip, not Jesus, so it takes no setting.

decisions.choice: Do you not believe ...?: a question that expects "yes"
decisions.reason: "You" is still singular, spoken to Philip. The form of the question expects agreement: Philip does believe this, at least in part, and should see what follows from it.

decisions.choice: I am in the Father and the Father is in me: the closest unity, while each stays distinct
decisions.reason: Jesus said this to the crowd in Jerusalem (10:38), and he will pray that his followers may share in it (17:21-23). The Father and the Son are two, since one is in the other, yet so close that to see the Son is to see the Father (verse 9). The next sentence shows how this is seen: in Jesus's words and works.

decisions.choice: Philip, surely you believe ...?
decisions.reason: Readable names Philip because the English "you" does not show that Jesus is still speaking to him alone, and "surely" shows that the question expects "yes" (meaning decision m1); the plural "you" returns in the next sentence.

decisions.choice: Felipe, tú crees ..., ¿no es así?
decisions.reason: As in English: the question expects yes (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: dans le Père ... en moi
decisions.reason: The Greek uses one preposition in both halves (meaning decision m2). French "en" cannot stand before "le", and "au Père" would mean "to the Father", so French says "dans le Père" and "en moi", which carry the same sense. The same pair is used in verse 11 and wherever the phrase returns.

decisions.choice: "아버지께서 ... 계신다" but "내가 ... 있다"
decisions.reason: Jesus gives the Father the honorific "께서" and "계시다", but does not honour himself in his own speech; Korean must mark this difference where the Greek has one verb for both.

decisions.choice: from myself: on my own initiative and authority
decisions.reason: Jesus says again and again that he does and says nothing on his own (5:19, 30; 7:16-18; 8:28; 12:49-50). His words come from the Father who sent him. Two verbs for "say" and "speak" are used; here they mean the same.

decisions.choice: words ... works: Jesus's words are among the Father's works
alternatives: two separate statements, one about words and one about works
decisions.reason: One would expect "the Father speaks the words", but the sentence moves from words to works. Jesus's words and his deeds are one work of the Father, done through him. This leads into verse 11: believe because of the works.

decisions.choice: remains: stays and lives in me
decisions.reason: The verb is the one John uses for lasting union (6:56; 15:4-10), and it is the verb behind the "dwelling places" of verse 2. The Father does not visit Jesus from time to time; he remains in him.

decisions.choice: on my own authority (B); do not come from me on my own (R); remains (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "on my own authority" as in 12:49 (meaning decision m1). "Remains" is the book-wide word for this verb in its theological sense, kept at every level so the link with 15:4-10 can be seen (meaning decision m3). Readable makes the Father the subject of a new sentence.

decisions.choice: permanece; por mi propia autoridad (B)
decisions.reason: "Permanecer" for the weighty sense of remaining (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: demeure, at every level
decisions.reason: The book-wide French word for this verb in its theological sense (meaning decision m3), kept at every level as the English keeps "remains". It also shares its root with the "demeures" of verse 2, as the Greek verb and noun do, and leads to "demeurez en moi" in 15:4-10.

decisions.choice: anakaa / anayekaa (remains)
decisions.reason: "Kukaa" for this verb throughout John, so that "remain" stays one word for the reader (also verses 17 and 25). "Kwa nafsi yangu" (from myself) at Literal, as at 12:49.

decisions.choice: ở lại
decisions.reason: "Ở lại" is the book-wide word for menō in its theological sense (remain), so the thread through 15:4-10 stays visible.

source.text: πιστεύετέ μοι ὅτι ἐγὼ ἐν τῷ πατρὶ καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ἐν ἐμοί· εἰ δὲ μή, διὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτὰ πιστεύετε.

records.literal_gloss: Believe me that I [am] in the Father and the Father in me; if but not, because of the works themselves believe.

en.L: Believe {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} that I [am] in the Father and the Father in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; but if not, believe because of the works themselves.
en.B: Believe {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}: I am in the Father, and the Father is in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. If not, then believe because of the works themselves.
en.R: All of you, believe {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}: I am in the Father, and the Father is in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. If you cannot believe {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, then believe because of the works themselves, the things you have seen {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} do.

es.L: {{plural_you:Créanme|Creedme}} que yo [estoy] en el Padre y el Padre en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}; y si no, {{plural_you:crean|creed}} por las obras mismas.
es.B: {{plural_you:Créanme|Creedme}}: yo estoy en el Padre, y el Padre está en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Y si no, {{plural_you:crean|creed}} por las obras mismas.
es.R: {{plural_you:Créanme todos ustedes|Creedme todos vosotros}}: yo estoy en el Padre, y el Padre está en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Si no {{plural_you:pueden creerme|podéis creerme}}, {{plural_you:crean|creed}} al menos por las obras mismas, por lo que me {{plural_you:han visto|habéis visto}} hacer.

fr.L: Croyez-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} : je [suis] dans le Père, et le Père en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ; mais sinon, croyez à cause des œuvres elles-mêmes.
fr.B: Croyez-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} : je suis dans le Père, et le Père est en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Sinon, croyez du moins à cause de ces œuvres elles-mêmes.
fr.R: Croyez-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} : je suis dans le Père, et le Père est en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Si vous ne pouvez pas {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} croire sur parole, alors croyez à cause des œuvres elles-mêmes, ce que vous {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}avez vu faire.

sw.L: Niaminini kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} [niko] ndani ya Baba na Baba ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}; la sivyo, aminini kwa sababu ya kazi zenyewe.
sw.B: Niaminini: niko ndani ya Baba, na Baba yuko ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. La sivyo, aminini kwa sababu ya kazi zenyewe.
sw.R: Ninyi nyote, niaminini: niko ndani ya Baba, na Baba yuko ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Kama hamwezi kuniamini, basi aminini kwa sababu ya kazi zenyewe, yale mliyoniona nikiyafanya.

vi.L: Hãy tin {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} [ở] trong Cha và Cha [ở] trong {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; nhưng nếu không, thì hãy tin vì chính các công việc ấy.
vi.B: Hãy tin {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}: {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở trong Cha, và Cha ở trong {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Nếu không, thì hãy tin vì chính những công việc ấy.
vi.R: Tất cả các con hãy tin {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}: {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở trong Cha, và Cha ở trong {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Nếu các con không thể tin {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, thì hãy tin vì chính những việc các con đã thấy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm.

ko.L: 나를 믿어라, 내가 아버지 안에 [있고] 아버지께서 내 안에 [계신다는 것을]. 그렇지 않다면 그 일들 자체 때문에 믿어라.
ko.B: 내 말을 믿어라. 나는 아버지 안에 있고, 아버지께서는 내 안에 계신다. 그렇지 않다면 내가 하는 일들 그 자체를 보고서라도 믿어라.
ko.R: 너희 모두 내 말을 믿어라. 나는 아버지 안에 있고, 아버지께서는 내 안에 계신다. 내 말을 믿을 수 없다면, 내가 하는 일들을 보고서라도 믿어라. 너희는 그 일들을 직접 보았다.

decisions.choice: Believe me ... believe: commands to all the disciples
decisions.reason: The verb is now plural: Jesus turns from Philip to the whole group. Both verbs are commands. "Believe me" means to trust what Jesus says, on his word.

decisions.choice: if not: if you will not believe on my word alone
decisions.reason: The words left out are easy to supply from what comes before: if they do not believe what he says, they can believe because of what he does.

decisions.choice: the works themselves: the signs and deeds the Father does through Jesus
decisions.reason: In John, Jesus's "works" are all he does at the Father's bidding, including the signs (5:36; 9:3-4; 10:25, 32, 37-38). They bear witness to who he is. Jesus said the same to his opponents in 10:37-38. Faith that rests on the works is a first step, not the last (compare 20:29).

decisions.choice: Believe me: I am in the Father (B, R); All of you (R); If you cannot believe me (R); the things you have seen me do (R)
alternatives: Believe me that I am in the Father
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable set out what Jesus asks them to believe after a colon. Readable says "All of you" because the English "you" does not show the change from singular to plural (meaning decision m1), spells out "if not" (meaning decision m2), and explains "works" by what the disciples have seen (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: Créanme / Creedme
decisions.reason: Commands to all the disciples (meaning decision m1); the clitic "me" sits inside the span with the verb.

decisions.choice: Croyez-moi, without "Vous tous"
alternatives: Vous tous, croyez-moi (as the English "All of you")
decisions.reason: The English Readable adds "All of you" because English "you" does not show the turn from Philip to the whole group (meaning decision m1). In French the plural "croyez" after "tu crois" already shows it. Readable adds "sur parole" to say what believing him on his word means.

decisions.choice: "내 말을 믿어라" (B, R); "나를 믿어라" (L)
decisions.reason: With the dative, "believe me" means trust what I say; Korean "내 말을 믿다" says that, and keeps it apart from "나를 믿다" (believe in me, 14:1, 12).

source.text: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ τὰ ἔργα ἃ ἐγὼ ποιῶ κἀκεῖνος ποιήσει, καὶ μείζονα τούτων ποιήσει, ὅτι ἐγὼ πρὸς τὸν πατέρα πορεύομαι·

records.literal_gloss: Truly truly I say to you, the [one] believing in me the works that I do also that one will do, and greater [than] these he will do, because I to the Father am going;

en.L: Truly, truly I say to you, the one who believes in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, the works that I do, that one also will do; and greater [works] than these {{gender:they|he}} will do, because I am going to the Father.
en.B: Truly, truly, I tell you, anyone who believes in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will also do the works I am doing, and will do greater works than these, since I am going to the Father.
en.R: I tell you the truth: anyone who believes in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will do the same works I do. In fact, {{gender:they|he}} will do even greater works than these, because I am going to the Father.

es.L: En verdad, en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: el que cree en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, las obras que yo hago, también {{gender:esa persona|él}} las hará; y [obras] mayores que estas hará, porque yo voy al Padre.
es.B: En verdad, en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que el que cree en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} también hará las obras que yo hago, y hará obras mayores que estas, porque yo voy al Padre.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: el que cree en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} hará las mismas obras que yo hago. Incluso hará obras mayores que estas, porque yo voy al Padre.

fr.L: En vérité, en vérité, je vous le dis, celui qui croit en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, les œuvres que je fais, celui-là aussi les fera ; et il en fera de plus grandes que celles-ci, parce que je vais vers le Père.
fr.B: En vérité, en vérité, je vous le dis, quiconque croit en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} fera aussi les œuvres que je fais, et en fera de plus grandes encore, puisque je vais vers le Père.
fr.R: Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité : celui qui croit en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} fera les mêmes œuvres que je fais. Et même, il fera des œuvres encore plus grandes, parce que je vais vers le Père.

sw.L: Kweli kweli nawaambia, anayeniamini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, kazi ninazozifanya {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, yeye naye atazifanya; na kubwa kuliko hizi atafanya, kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninakwenda kwa Baba.
sw.B: Kweli kweli nawaambia, yeyote anayeniamini atazifanya pia kazi ninazozifanya, naye atafanya kazi kubwa kuliko hizi, kwa kuwa ninakwenda kwa Baba.
sw.R: Nawaambia ukweli: yeyote anayeniamini atafanya kazi zile zile ninazofanya. Kwa kweli, atafanya hata kazi kubwa zaidi kuliko hizi, kwa sababu ninakwenda kwa Baba.

vi.L: Thật vậy, thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, người nào tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, những việc {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm, người ấy cũng sẽ làm; và [những việc] lớn hơn những việc này người ấy sẽ làm, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi đến cùng Cha.
vi.B: Thật vậy, thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, ai tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì cũng sẽ làm những việc {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang làm, và sẽ làm những việc lớn hơn thế nữa, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi đến với Cha.
vi.R: Ta nói thật với các con: ai tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm được những việc {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm. Thật ra, người ấy còn sẽ làm những việc lớn hơn những việc này nữa, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi về với Cha.

ko.L: 진실로 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 나를 믿는 사람은, 내가 하는 일들을 그 사람도 할 것이고, 이것들보다 더 큰 [일들도] 할 것이다. 내가 아버지께로 가기 때문이다.
ko.B: 진실로 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 나를 믿는 사람은 내가 하는 일을 그도 할 것이고, 이보다 더 큰 일도 할 것이다. 내가 아버지께로 가기 때문이다.
ko.R: 내가 분명히 말한다. 나를 믿는 사람은 누구든지 내가 하는 일을 똑같이 할 것이다. 아니, 이보다 더 큰 일도 할 것이다. 내가 아버지께로 가기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: greater works: greater in reach, done after Jesus has gone to the Father
alternatives: more astonishing miracles than Jesus did
decisions.reason: The reason given is "because I am going to the Father". After his going, Jesus will send the Spirit (7:39; 16:7), and through the disciples' witness the life he gives will reach far beyond the few places and people of his own ministry (4:35-38; 10:16; 17:20; 20:21-23). That seems to be the sense: greater in scope and in what they bring about, not more spectacular miracles. The works are still his, done by the one who believes in him, as verses 13-14 go on to say.

decisions.choice: the one who believes ... that one also: any believer, man or woman
decisions.reason: "The one who believes" means anyone at all who believes in Jesus, not only the apostles in the room. The emphatic "that one also" points back to this believer and puts the stress on the person: the believer too will do what Jesus does.

decisions.choice: because I am going to the Father: Jesus's going makes the greater works possible
decisions.reason: His going away is not a loss for the work but the reason for its growth. He says the same of the Spirit's coming (16:7).

decisions.choice: Truly, truly I say to you (L); Truly, truly, I tell you (B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering for John (see 1:51), recorded once in this passage.

decisions.choice: greater [works] (L); greater works (B, R); even (R); they / he (L, R)
decisions.reason: "Greater" in the Greek has no noun; "works" is supplied from the first half of the verse. Where English needs a pronoun for the believer, the reader's gender setting gives "they" or "he"; Balanced needs none. Readable adds "In fact" and "even" to mark the step up from "the same works" to "greater works".

decisions.choice: En verdad, en verdad les digo (L, B); Les digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering.

decisions.choice: {{gender:esa persona|él}}
decisions.reason: Any believer, man or woman (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps the emphatic "that one also", so it needs a pronoun, which takes the gender setting; Balanced and Readable need none.

decisions.choice: En vérité, en vérité, je vous le dis (L, B); Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité (R)
alternatives: Amen, amen, je vous le dis
Oui, vraiment, je vous le dis
decisions.reason: The book-wide French rendering for John (see 1:51), recorded once in this passage.

decisions.choice: celui qui ... celui-là ... il (L, R); quiconque (B); no gender setting
alternatives: {{gender:la personne|celui}} ... {{gender:elle|il}}, putting the whole chain under the setting
decisions.reason: Any believer, man or woman (meaning decision m2). French "celui qui", "quiconque" and "quelqu’un" already speak of anyone, man or woman, and the pronouns that refer back to them ("il", "lui", "celui-là") are the ordinary generic forms, so French needs no gender setting where the English needs one for "he" or "they". The setting is kept for nouns French has to choose (docs/french-style.md §7).

decisions.choice: yeye naye / atafanya, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English needs "they" with "he" as the traditional alternative; Swahili "yeye" and the verb prefix "a-" say nothing about sex, so there is no span here or in verses 21 and 23, as at 12:25.

decisions.choice: Thật vậy, thật vậy, Ta nói với các con (L, B); Ta nói thật với các con (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide form of "Truly, truly". Recorded once for this passage.

decisions.choice: người ấy, with no gender span
decisions.reason: Where the English offers "they" or "he", Vietnamese "người ấy" (that person) already includes men and women, so no gender setting is needed.

decisions.choice: "진실로 진실로 너희에게 말한다" (L, B); "내가 분명히 말한다" (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide Korean rendering of amen amen (style guide, section 6), recorded once for this passage.

decisions.choice: no gender span: "그 사람도" (L), "그도" (B), "누구든지" (R)
alternatives: gender setting spans as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean "사람", "그" and "누구든지" already include men and women (style guide, section 7), so the gender setting has nothing to change here.

source.text: καὶ ὅ τι ἂν αἰτήσητε ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου τοῦτο ποιήσω, ἵνα δοξασθῇ ὁ πατὴρ ἐν τῷ υἱῷ·

records.literal_gloss: And whatever you may ask in the name of me, this I will do, so that may be glorified the Father in the Son;

en.L: And whatever you ask in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, this I will do, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
en.B: And whatever you ask in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, I will do it, so that in the Son the Father may be glorified.
en.R: I will do anything you ask for in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. That way the Father's glory will be shown in the Son.

es.L: Y todo lo que {{plural_you:pidan|pidáis}} en mi nombre, eso haré, para que el Padre sea glorificado en el Hijo.
es.B: Y todo lo que {{plural_you:pidan|pidáis}} en mi nombre, yo lo haré, para que en el Hijo sea glorificado el Padre.
es.R: Haré todo lo que {{plural_you:pidan|pidáis}} en mi nombre. Así se mostrará en el Hijo la gloria del Padre.

fr.L: Et tout ce que vous demanderez en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, cela je le ferai, afin que le Père soit glorifié dans le Fils.
fr.B: Et quoi que vous demandiez en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, je le ferai, pour que dans le Fils le Père soit glorifié.
fr.R: Je ferai tout ce que vous demanderez en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom. Ainsi, la gloire du Père se montrera dans le Fils.

sw.L: Na chochote mtakachoomba kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, hicho nitakifanya, ili Baba apate kutukuzwa katika Mwana.
sw.B: Na lolote mtakaloomba kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, nitalitimiza, ili ndani ya Mwana Baba atukuzwe.
sw.R: Nitafanya chochote mtakachoomba kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}. Kwa njia hiyo utukufu wa Baba utaonekana ndani ya Mwana.

vi.L: Và bất cứ điều gì các con cầu xin trong danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, điều ấy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm, để Cha được tôn vinh trong Con.
vi.B: Và bất cứ điều gì các con nhân danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} mà cầu xin, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm điều đó, để Cha được tôn vinh trong Con.
vi.R: Ta sẽ làm bất cứ điều gì các con nhân danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} mà cầu xin. Như vậy, vinh quang của Cha sẽ được bày tỏ trong Con.

ko.L: 그리고 너희가 내 이름으로 무엇을 구하든지, 이것을 내가 행할 것이다. 아버지께서 아들 안에서 영광스럽게 되시도록 하려는 것이다.
ko.B: 너희가 내 이름으로 무엇을 구하든지 내가 그것을 이루어 주겠다. 그리하여 아버지께서 아들 안에서 영광스럽게 되시게 하려는 것이다.
ko.R: 너희가 내 이름으로 구하는 것은 무엇이든지 내가 해 주겠다. 그렇게 해서 아들 안에서 아버지의 영광이 드러나게 하려는 것이다.

decisions.choice: in my name: as people who belong to Jesus, by his authority and in keeping with who he is
alternatives: simply saying his name at the end of a prayer
decisions.reason: A name stands for the person. To ask in Jesus's name is to ask as his disciples, joined to him, on the ground of what he is and does, and so for what he would want. It is not a form of words that makes any request certain. This is the first time Jesus speaks of asking in his name; he returns to it in 15:16 and 16:23-26.

decisions.choice: whatever you ask ... I will do it: Jesus himself answers
decisions.reason: The verse does not say whom they ask; verse 14 says "ask me", and 15:16 and 16:23 speak of asking the Father. Here the stress is that Jesus, though going to the Father, will still act for his disciples. This is how the "greater works" of verse 12 will be done.

decisions.choice: so that the Father may be glorified in the Son: the purpose of Jesus's answering
decisions.reason: When Jesus does what his disciples ask, the Father's glory is shown in what the Son does, as it was in his signs (11:4, 40) and will be in his death (13:31-32). Everything leads back to the Father.

decisions.choice: so that in the Son the Father may be glorified (B); That way the Father's glory will be shown in the Son (R)
alternatives: so that the Father may be glorified in the Son
decisions.reason: Balanced puts "in the Son" first, as it put "in him" first in 13:31, to keep the stress on the Son. Readable says that the Father's glory "will be shown", as it did in 13:31, which is what being glorified means here.

decisions.choice: en el Hijo sea glorificado el Padre (B); se mostrará en el Hijo la gloria del Padre (R)
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: trong danh Ta (L); nhân danh Ta (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the preposition "in"; Balanced and Readable use "nhân danh" (in the name of, by the authority of), the natural Vietnamese for acting on someone's authority.

decisions.choice: "구하다" for "ask"
decisions.reason: "구하다" is asking for something from one who can give it, as in prayer; "요구하다" would sound like a demand, and "기도하다" narrows the verb.

source.text: ἐάν τι αἰτήσητέ με ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου ἐγὼ ποιήσω.

records.literal_gloss: If anything you may ask me in the name of me, I will do.

en.L: If you ask {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} anything in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, I will do [it].
en.B: If you ask {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} anything in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will do it.
en.R: Yes, ask {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for anything in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will do it.

es.L: Si me {{plural_you:piden|pedís}} algo en mi nombre, yo [lo] haré.
es.B: Si me {{plural_you:piden|pedís}} algo en mi nombre, yo mismo lo haré.
es.R: Sí, {{plural_you:pídanme|pedidme}} cualquier cosa en mi nombre, y yo mismo lo haré.

fr.L: Si vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} demandez quelque chose en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je [le] ferai.
fr.B: Si vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} demandez quoi que ce soit en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, je le ferai {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}}.
fr.R: Oui, demandez-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} quoi que ce soit en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, et je le ferai {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}}.

sw.L: Ikiwa mtaniomba kitu kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nitakifanya.
sw.R: Ndiyo, niombeni chochote kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} nitakifanya.

vi.L: Nếu các con xin {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} điều gì trong danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm [điều đó].
vi.B: Nếu các con nhân danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} mà xin {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} điều gì, chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm điều đó.

ko.L: 너희가 내 이름으로 나에게 무엇을 구하면, 내가 [그것을] 행할 것이다.

decisions.choice: ask me: the word "me" is read
alternatives: If you ask anything in my name, I will do it
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts lack "me", giving "If you ask anything in my name"; this may have been an attempt to fit the verse to 16:23, where the disciples ask the Father. A few manuscripts and early versions lack the whole verse, probably because it seemed to repeat verse 13. The SBLGNT includes the verse with "me", and the oldest manuscripts support it. A reviewer should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: ask me ... I will do it: prayer to Jesus himself, answered by him
decisions.reason: The disciples may ask Jesus himself, and the "I" is stressed: he himself will act. Later he speaks of asking the Father in his name (15:16; 16:23); John holds both together, since the Father and the Son are one in their work (verse 10).

decisions.choice: I myself will do it (B, R); Yes, ask me for anything ..., and (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "I myself" for the stressed "I" (meaning decision m2). Readable begins with "Yes" to show that Jesus is repeating and stressing the promise of verse 13, and turns the condition into an invitation, which in English says the same thing.

decisions.choice: yo mismo (B, R); Sí, pídanme (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Jesus himself answers (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je [le] ferai
decisions.reason: The "I" is stressed (meaning decision m2). Literal shows it with the stressed "moi" before "je", which as a pronoun for Christ takes the deity_pronoun setting; Balanced and Readable say "moi-même", as the English says "I myself". French needs an object for "faire", which Literal brackets.
